title: Update a running install safely, and undo it when the update goes wrong
contract: A five-phase `hermes update` pipeline with `--check` (preview), `--plan` (fleet preview), `--branch NAME`, parked-branch strategy, a stash-vs-discard policy for non-interactive runs, machine-readable update receipts plus a post-restart fleet version check that each gateway actually serves the new code, opt-in pre-update backup of the whole HERMES_HOME, Windows transactional-venv guards, SIGHUP survival with update.log, a documented manual rollback to any commit/tag, a clean refusal on image-managed (Docker/Nix/apt) installs, and `/update` from Telegram/Discord/Slack (16 entries: docs-rest.update-*).
governance: privileged and irreversible — pulling and executing new code is host execution. It must cross the kernel; the `repo.sync` kind already exists and is already default-refused when the kernel is off (agents/core/kernel/registry.py, agents/core/plugins/oracle_bridge.py:58), so extend it (or mint `host.update` next to it) and route the apply phase into the irreversible half of the approval queue. `--check`/`--plan`/receipts stay read-only.
remaining_verbatim:
- --branch / parked-branch strategy and a settable tracked branch (the target is the pinned commit, the tracked upstream, or a tag/branch/sha given per request)
- discard policy for a dirty tree (only refuse or stash are offered, by design)
- SIGHUP survival and an update.log file outside the receipt (the log lives in the receipt and the action)
- /update from channels (Telegram/Discord/Slack)
- the apply step does not cross the Action Kernel (repo.sync / host.update); it is gated by the irreversible approval tier only
- schema migrations run when stores open after the restart; the plan flags store code by path and content (conservatively), it does not know which migrations will run
- targets are not bound to a branch or tag pattern the owner pins: any trusted commit that fast-forwards HEAD is accepted
- a release whose serve.py itself fails before the guard runs cannot roll itself back; the standard-library fallback in serve.py does not reinstall dependencies or restore data (the receipt ends rollback_incomplete and names what to run)
- a frontend change is reported (rebuild the HUD) but not built: npm would run package scripts
- Windows: the boot-guard rollback does not re-execute; the next start runs the previous code
- release-bundle (non-git) installs and fleet (multi-gateway) version checks
